caption:
😳🔴 A boil isn't just a bump...

It's a pocket of pus forming beneath your skin.

Boils develop when bacteria infect a **hair follicle** or nearby oil gland. Your immune system responds by sending white blood cells to fight the infection, leading to a buildup of pus.

⚠️ As pressure increases, the area becomes red, swollen, warm, and painful.

💡 Most boils heal with proper treatment, but large, recurrent, or spreading boils should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.

#Boils #SkinInfection
on_screen_hook: A boil doesn't suddenly appear. It starts when bacteria get trapped deep
transcript: A boil doesn't suddenly appear. It starts when bacteria get trapped deep inside a hair follicle. Your immune system immediately attacks the bacteria. White blood cells flood the area. But as they die along with bacteria and damaged tissue, a thick pocket of pus begins to form beneath the skin. As more pus builds up, stretches the skin, causing pain and swelling. Eventually, the boil drains, releasing the trapped pus and allowing the infection to begin healing.

title: How To Get Rid of Acne Scars
caption:
Those red spots, dark patches, and small indentations left behind by acne aren't all scars - and that matters for treatment. Plus the one step you can't skip before addressing any scarring.

Brought to you by ‪@cerave‬ .
transcript: How do you get rid of acne scars? Well, first you need to know, are they actual scars or just marks? Those red or dark spots, those are just acne marks. Arythemma means red. Hyperpigmentation means dark. Because they're not scars, they usually just fade with time. But those little dents or divots in your skin, those are true acne scars called atrophic scars, and they go much deeper. But here's the real problem. Popping pimples causes scarring because you push that gunk deeper. So, it causes inflammation further under the skin, which triggers scarring. But before you can get rid of your scars, you have to treat your acne. Treating scars while you're still breaking out is like mopping the floor while the faucet's still running. But if you want to get started at home, topical retinoids are your best at home option because they fight acne, reduce post acne marks, and improve scarring.

caption:
Tried antifungal treatment for light patches with no improvement?

The diagnosis might be the problem.

#progressivemacularhypomelanosis #skintok #skincaretips #vitiligo #dermatologist
on_screen_hook: This is not a yeast infection, and it's not vitiligo either. This
transcript: This is not a yeast infection, and it's not vitiligo either. This is progressive macular hypomelanosis. It appears as smooth like patches on the chest, back, or abdomen, and is often confused for pityriasis versicolor. But unlike pityriasis versicolor, it isn't caused by a yeast. Pigment loss is thought to be linked to Cutibacterium acnes disrupting melanin production. Treatment includes benzoyl peroxide, topical antibiotics, and for more persistent cases, phototherapy. So if you've been treating light patches with antifungal creams and shampoos and nothing is changing, you could have the wrong diagnosis.

title: How is Cosmetic Mole Removal Performed?
caption:
Do you Know the Different Options for Cosmetic Mole Removal? Dr. Tzu, triple board-certified dermatologist, discusses the three main procedures utilized to remove moles for aesthetic purposes  💉✨

Learn More About Mole Removal at Wall Street Dermatology in New York City:
https://www.wallstreetdermatology.com/mole-removal/

⭐ Want more tips for your perfect look? Check out our other videos: www.youtube.com/@NYCdermatologist-juliatzu

⭐ Don’t miss out on the fun—follow us on our socials for update
transcript: How is cosmetic mole removal performed? I'm a board-certified dermatologic surgeon. I've removed over 10,000 moles in my practice and these are the three main ways in which I remove moles for cosmetic purposes. Number one, laser mole removal. Now, this procedure is generally reserved for moles that are more superficial. So, smaller, lighter in color and flat. Now, a dermatologist needs to first verify that these moles are completely benign before they're able to be safely removed by laser. Number two, shave removal. Now, this procedure is generally reserved for moles that are bumpy because the surgical blade is used to cut across the base of the mole, flattening it out just like the rest of your skin. Now, it's important to remember that shave removal doesn't guarantee that the mole won't grow back because the base of the mole may still be present. Number three, surgical excision. Now, this is a little bit more complicated of a procedure and is generally reserved for moles where patients want it completely gone and out. So, surgical blade is used to cut out the entirety of the mole along with a little bit of normal skin and the sides of the skin are then stitched together which forms a small line scar. Now, the appearance of the scar will eventually fade with time so that the ultimate appearance of the scar is much less visible than the original mole itself. Have a conversation with their dermatologist to see which procedure is right for your mole. [Music]

caption: I talk all the time about doing MOHS reconstruction, and I forget that maybe not everybody knows what the heck that even is! MOHS surgery is a technique performed by highly trained surgeons, usually sub specialized dermatologists, to remove skin cancer. Then I come in and reconstruct the defect with the goal of returning the patient as close to their original appearance as I can.  #mohs #skincancer #skincancerawareness #skincare #beauty #mohssurgery
on_screen_hook: So I realized I post quite a bit about doing Mo's reconstruction
transcript: So I realized I post quite a bit about doing Mo's reconstruction and kind of came to the realization I haven't really described what Mo's surgery is so specifically. It's called Mohs micrographic excision. And it's a technique developed by Doctor Frederick Mohs, I believe it's back in the 50s at the university of Wisconsin. Anyway, it's, um, it's a real time analysis of the tumor as it comes off in three dimensions. So it's not only going around the, uh, skin cancer in question, it's going under it. And then with each what's called layer being removed, it's immediately evaluated by the most surgeon who is trained dermatopathologist or a skin, uh, pathologist. And so they look at it right underneath the microscope right then and there, and they continue to go down. You can see here that only this little yellow spot is the remaining tumor. So they go to here, they get most of it out, but they see just a little bit is still left. So then over here, they just focus on that one area. So with this three dimensional tumor mapping, they have a very high degree of clearance, a relatively low degree of collateral damage, and a very low degree of recurrent disease. So it's actually the gold standard for basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, the area in which I specialize for reconstruction. It also can be used in some forms of melanoma for a specially trained Amount of pathologist. And then what I do is I many times will come in and help to reconstruct the defect or the hole that is left over. So there's the difference. And just kind of a little factoids about that.
